text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- 1997 health care budget cuts funding to Paris public hospitals for better balance with provinces.
-- Danone halts sale of food products made with British beef as a result of French food inspection investigation.
-- GEC Alsthom picks up one billion franc contract from Belgium's Electrabel.
-- French construction equipment market down 12 percent in 1996 but industry expects Q2 upturn in 1997.
-- Air France adopts three-year plan to trim costs by 15 percent and boost competitive position.
-- Brussels approves 350 million franc cash injection to state-owned SFP film/TV programme production company prior to acquisition by Havas-Generale Des Eaux.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Paris stock market up 22.2 percent in 1996 -- best showing since 1993.
-- Finance minister Jean Arthuis remains non-commital over candidacy of Holland's Wim Duisenberg as the next chief of European Monetary Institute, a candidate backed by the Bundesbank.
L'AGEFI
-- Paris stock market up 24.7 percent in 1996.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Paris stock market up 24.7 percent in 1996 -- best showing since 1989.
-- Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet wants the euro to be as strong as the franc.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Car bomb explodes at headquarters of French national statistics bureau, hurting no one.
-- Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer expects 1997 French car market to shrink to 1.9 million units from 2.1 million.
LE PARISIEN
-- France delays imports of genetically-engineered corn with labelling requirements.
